findings.claim: The 15-second sign-in-exchange deadline is asserted without any stated source, while only the 30-second cap is traced to a canonical requirement.
findings.evidence: "One shared 15-second sign-in-exchange deadline should start before the sign-in write... The 30-second active cap comes from the canonical single-attempt frame-observation requirement and remains the outer bound" — the origin of the 15s value is never given (no prior-handoff citation, no canonical requirement reference), so Plan will propagate an untraceable magic number into the new OpenSpec delta it is instructed to create.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the prior child's accepted requirement or evidence from which the 15-second value derives, or explicitly flag it as a new value Plan must justify in the delta.

findings.claim: Line-precise behavioral claims about collector.mjs are unverifiable from the packet and, if wrong, will misdirect the Plan-stage copy-and-modify step.
findings.evidence: "`collector.mjs:271-303` can send a masked Text RPC and parse one nonempty final unmasked Text response. It rejects the observed `0x89 0x00` structure at line 285 and would reject length zero at line 293" — the file tree contains no collector.mjs contents and `prior_handoffs` is null, so nothing in the packet corroborates these line numbers; minimum boundary item 1 ("Copy the diagnostic collector into this child") depends on them being accurate.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the actual rejecting conditionals from collector.mjs rather than bare line numbers, or mark the line citations as to-be-reverified at Plan time.

findings.claim: The boundary does not state whether a zero-length Ping arriving before the sign-in write completes is in scope.
findings.evidence: Item 5 says "Continue to one subsequent final, RSV-clear, unmasked Text response under the original sign-in-exchange deadline. If Text is the first response, accept the existing path without sending Pong," and the deadline "start[s] before the sign-in write and cover[s] first-header read, Pong write and the single following response" — but the accept/stop rule is only defined for frames after the write; a Ping interleaved with the write itself is neither explicitly admitted nor explicitly a stop condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the boundary specifying whether the single-Ping allowance applies only after the sign-in write settles, or to any first header within the exchange window.
